text: @etby-studio/dsh-commands 是供 DSH 使用的文件系统斜杠命令插件：它接入 DSH 命令注册表，从默认命令目录和可配置的额外目录读取 Markdown 文件，并按文件名注册命令。每个文件用 YAML frontmatter 描述命令，正文作为模型指令；触发命令时可附加参数或替换正文中的参数占位符。目录监听会同步新增、修改和删除，适合希望用文件维护可复用提示命令的 DSH 用户。通过 dsh plugin add 安装，无需 API Key 或外部账号。

@etby-studio/dsh-commands loads DSH slash commands from Markdown files. Filenames name commands, frontmatter supplies descriptions, and file bodies become instructions. Watchers sync changes; arguments can be appended or substituted. Install with dsh plugin add; no API key is needed.
想把自己写的 Markdown 提示词做成 DSH 里能调用的斜杠命令
DSH 能不能自动从 commands 文件夹加载命令并在文件变化时更新？
I want DSH to discover reusable slash commands from Markdown files on disk.
@etby-studio/dsh-commands 的功能「文件命令发现」：扫描默认及额外命令目录，把符合格式的 Markdown 文件注册为斜杠命令；名称取自文件名，描述取自 YAML frontmatter，正文在调用时作为指令发送。
@etby-studio/dsh-commands 的功能「命令文件热更新」：监听命令目录中的新增、修改和删除事件并更新注册表；执行时重新读取正文，参数可追加到正文后，也可替换 `$ARGUMENTS` 占位符。

@etby-studio/dsh-commands README · dsh-commands：English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Filesystem slash-command discovery for DeepSeek Harness UIs.

@etby-studio/dsh-commands README · dsh-commands：This plugin registers one slash command per Markdown file under `<dshHome>/commands`, mirroring the user-root layout of the skill discovery in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem`. The filename stem is the command name, the YAML frontmatter supplies the description, and the body is the instruction executed when the command runs. A host watcher keeps registrations in sync with the directory: adding, editing, or deleting a command file updates the registry without a restart, and the registry's own `commands/change` event refreshes live discovery UIs.
@etby-studio/dsh-commands README · dsh-commands：It is a plugin for the DeepSeek Harness command registry (`ctx.commands`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-commands`).

@etby-studio/dsh-commands README · Install：From npm:

```sh
dsh plugin add @etby-studio/dsh-commands
```

Developing locally (the build output `lib/` is gitignored; build it first after cloning):

```sh
pnpm run build
dsh plugin add /path/to/dsh-commands
```

@etby-studio/dsh-commands README · Install：The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch` (`cordis.patch.yml`), so `dsh plugin add` installs it as a
profile layer and that layer inserts the plugin row itself — no manual `cordis.patch.yml` edit.
Do not also add the row to `$DSH_HOME/profiles/<name>/cordis.patch.yml`: a second insert of the
same id is a duplicate Loader entry.

@etby-studio/dsh-commands README · Install：`dsh plugin add` refuses packages without `dsh.bundle`, and DSH loads a bundle only when every
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peer range matches the runtime version, so this release targets
dsh `0.2.0-rc.2` (peers `^0.2.0-rc.2`).

After boot, any `*.md` file in `<dshHome>/commands` becomes a slash command (`dshHome` defaults to `$DSH_HOME` or `~/.dsh`).

@etby-studio/dsh-commands README · Command file format：Each command is one Markdown file; the filename stem (without `.md`) is the command name, lowercased ASCII with letters, digits, `_`, or `-`, matching `parseCommand()`:

```markdown
---
description: Execute the plan
---

@etby-studio/dsh-commands README · Steps：1. Review the plan
2. Create a task list
```

- `description` (required) — shown in command discovery UI.
- Body — the instruction submitted to the model when the command runs.

Invalid files (missing frontmatter, empty description, invalid name, empty body) are skipped with a warning and never registered.

@etby-studio/dsh-commands README · Execution：The handler never implicitly submits to the model. On `/name [args]` it reads the current body and steers one user message to the receiving agent:

- Typed arguments append after a blank line (`/go <description>` → body + blank line + `<description>`).
- A `$ARGUMENTS` placeholder in the body is substituted with the arguments instead.

The body is re-read at every execution, so file edits take effect without a restart.

@etby-studio/dsh-commands README · Conflicts：File commands are low priority: when a plugin has already registered the same name, the file is skipped with a warning and the programmatic registration wins (no backfill while it lives).

@etby-studio/dsh-commands README · Watcher：Existing roots are watched with Chokidar (realpathed anchor, `depth: 1`, `awaitWriteFinish` stability). A missing root is probed from the nearest existing ancestor with `fs.watchFile`, so creating `~/.dsh/commands` later still attaches. Root deletion unregisters everything and reverses to the probe; recreation rescans. `commands/change` is emitted by the registry itself.

@etby-studio/dsh-commands README · Config：| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `dshHome` | `$DSH_HOME` or `~/.dsh` | Config root; scans `commands` under it. |
| `commandDirs` | `[]` | Extra command roots scanned after `<dshHome>/commands`. |
| `watch` | `true` | Watch command roots for registry updates. |
| `watchUsePolling` | `false` | Use Chokidar polling instead of native events. |
| `watchStabilityThresholdMs` | `200` | Stable-write window for Chokidar events. |
| `watchPollIntervalMs` | `100` | Polling/stability and missing-path probe interval. |
| `watchFollowSymlinks` | `true` | Follow symbolic links while watching roots. |

@etby-studio/dsh-commands README · Development：```sh
pnpm install
pnpm run build     # tsc → lib/
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run test      # 30 tests: discovery, watcher, real Loader composition

`@deepseek-ai/*` packages are peer dependencies resolved from the dsh installation at runtime; the tests run against the published npm releases (currently dsh `0.2.0-rc.2`).
